entities.summary:
Johannes Alberti (1698–1762) was a Dutch Reformed theologian associated with the liberal, philologically alert currents of eighteenth-century Protestant scholarship in the Netherlands. Working in a republic famous for relative intellectual tolerance, he engaged biblical criticism, doctrinal controversy, and academic theology at a time when Remonstrant and orthodox Reformed traditions still argued over grace, Scripture, and confessional boundaries.

Alberti’s milieu prized learned clergy who could read Hebrew and Greek, dispute in Latin, and address an urban reading public. The Dutch Enlightenment did not abolish Calvinist structures, but it pressured them toward historical reading of the Bible and softer confessional polemics.

He thus represents the scholarly pastor-professor type of the Dutch eighteenth century: a mediator between confessional orthodoxy and emerging critical habits that later biblical scholarship would radicalise.
